text:
jess (support): FYI customer (ACME) reports duplicate calls and double billing. They see two completions for one user request. They think TS SDK retries are firing after AbortController aborts.

jess (support): Environment: Node 18.16, @redwood/js 2.4.1, undici 5.15.0. SDK retry config: { retries: 2, backoff: 'exponential', timeoutMs: 3000 }

jess (support): Repro snippet they gave:
```js
import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/js';
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.KEY, retry: { retries: 2 } });
const ac = new AbortController();
setTimeout(() => ac.abort(), 2500);
await client.text.generate({ model: 'open-100', input: 'hello' , signal: ac.signal });
```

jess (support): Server logs show two accepted requests ~500ms apart and two billing events. Client logs show abort -> retry -> success.

emma (customer): here's the raw client logs we saw: 
```
[0] Sending request id=R1 payload=...
[2500] AbortSignal fired for id=R1 -> abort controller
[2510] retrying request (1/2) id=R2
[3010] 200 OK id=R2
```
Server shows:
```
[0] incoming req id=X1 processing
[600] incoming req id=X2 processing
```
We don't set idempotency keys.

alex (eng-sre): thanks. quick Qs: can you paste the raw request headers (x-request-id, x-redwood-retry)? Also is the SDK attaching different request ids per attempt? If the first request reached the model router but abort triggered locally, the runtime might still process it -> duplicate.

jess (support): pasted headers from client: 
```
x-request-id: 20260322-abc123
x-sdk-version: redwood-js/2.4.1
user-agent: redwood-js/2.4.1 node/18.16
```
Server trace shows two different x-request-id values (abc123 and def456) for the two arrivals. So SDK is sending a fresh id per retry.

sam (eng-runtime): this matches an expected behavior: when AbortController aborts, undici/Fetch sometimes cancels the request locally but TCP already sent, server may process it. SDK then issues a retry with a new request id. Without an idempotency key on the request body, server treats it as a second independent call.

sam (eng-runtime): short-term mitigations:
- recommend customers set an idempotency key header for non-idempotent operations if they want de-duplication (we can expose this in the SDK)
- reduce client-side abort aggressiveness (bump timeoutMs)
- set retries: 0 until we patch

sam (eng-runtime): longer-term: add an idempotency helper in TS SDK that generates a stable key per logical request and attach same key across retries; also consider propagating a 'retried-from' header when retrying after abort so runtime can dedupe.

jess (support): customer asked for immediate repro steps we can run locally. I created a minimal script that toggles undici's behavior and runs 10 loops. Sharing:
```bash
# install exact deps to match customer
npm init -y
npm i @redwood/js@2.4.1 undici@5.15.0
node repro.js
```
repro.js:
```js
const { RedwoodClient } = require('@redwood/js');
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.KEY, retry: { retries: 2 } });
async function run(){
  for(let i=0;i<10;i++){
    const ac = new AbortController();
    setTimeout(()=>ac.abort(), 2500);
    try{
      await client.text.generate({ model:'open-100', input:'ping' , signal: ac.signal });
      console.log('response ok', i);
    }catch(e){
      console.log('error', e.name || e.message);
    }
  }
}
run();
```

jess (support): when we ran this with a test backend that echoes, we saw ~20 incoming requests for 10 attempts.

alex (eng-sre): can you also try with undici 5.17 or node 20? Sometimes underlying fetch cancellation timing changed. But it sounds like expected network race.

emma (customer): we tried node20 and saw similar behaviour but less frequent. Would love a config flag to keep the same id across retries.

sam (eng-runtime): action items:
- I will prototype an idempotency header in SDK (expose `idempotencyKey` option) and a retry-mode toggle to reuse keys across attempts.
- Add docs note about AbortController + retries causing duplicate processing and recommend idempotency for billing-sensitive endpoints.
- engineering ticket created: INF-4923 (infra-bot created) :eyes:

infra-bot: Ticket INF-4923 created by sam. Priority: P2.

jess (support): sent customer a workaround: set retry:0 or add an idempotencyKey header per logical request. They confirmed disabling retries reduces duplicates. :white_check_mark:

alex (eng-sre): PSA for ops: if you see billing spikes correlate with client-side timeouts, this race is likely cause. Recommend checking for repeated model request patterns with different x-request-id but same user/timestamp window.

emma (customer): thanks all, we'll test idempotencyKey patch when it's available. Appreciate quick turnaround. :pray:

sam (eng-runtime): I'll post a follow-up PR and a small patch note once we have the SDK change and a test harness to simulate abort+retry.

jess (support): marking this thread resolved for now; will reopen if customer sees duplicates after applying workarounds. :thumbsup:
